newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN envoy to visit Zaire to probe massacre reports.
newsitem.headline: UN envoy to visit Zaire to probe massacre reports.

text.p: A United Nations special human rights investigator will visit Zaire in the coming weeks to look into reports of alleged massacres in the rebel-controlled east.
The investigator, Roberto Garreton, expressed concern over the crisis in east Zaire in a statement and said he would head for the region pending permission from the capital Kinshasa.

Garreton said he received many charges of extremely grave human rights violations in areas taken by mainly Tutsi rebels, who began fighting in October to topple president Mobutu Sese Seko and now control much of the east of the vast country.

Zaire's main human rights group, the Association for the Defence of Human Rights in Zaire (Azadho), has alleged large-scale massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees by the rebels at Mugunga, Kibumba, and Katale camps.
It has cited dates, places, witnesses and grave sites to back charges against the rebels and their alleged Rwandan and Ugandan army backers.
Rwanda and Uganda have denied any of their troops are involved in the fighting in east Zaire.

Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutus fled to eastern Zaire and Tanzania after Tutsi-led forces seized power in 1994 to halt genocidal killings of Tutsis and moderate Hutus by the Hutu-dominated army.
Many of the refugees, who had been used as human shields by Hutu troops fleeing the victorious Tutsis, have returned to Rwanda.
Others, caught between Zairean government forces and Tutsi-led rebels in east Zaire, have hidden in the dense forests or, weakened by disease and hunger, are staying in refugee camps.
